messages:
ops_bot: INCIDENT ALERT — sfo1 egress failures detected (pagerduty triggered). Routing errors and connection resets observed from multiple edge nodes.
pagerduty: PagerDuty: on-call escalation to ben_sre (critical).
ben_sre: on it. looking at host telemetry, beginning triage. can someone post the scope?
sofia: @ben_sre initial reports from monitoring: ~30% of sfo1 egress connections failing to upstream peers, spikes at 10:03 UTC. Some customers seeing 502-like errors.
alice_ops: +1 seeing elevated retry rates in sfo1. Autoscale bounced a few workers. no CPU or mem anomalies on hosts themselves.
ben_sre: pulling netflow and nat gateway metrics. suspect upstream peering / eBGP flap or transit congestion.
chris_support: we already have two customer tickets opened (C-2048, C-2051) reporting request timeouts and partial responses. Both marked high.
ellen_pm: impacted features: hosted inference + embeddings in sfo1 region only. Dedicated/private deployments not affected if they route outside sfo1.
sofia: quick customer-impact summary for status page: "Partial egress failures from sfo1 causing request errors and increased retries for some customers in western US."
ben_sre: confirmed multiple BGP neighbor resets around 10:02-10:04 UTC. Working with transit provider (AS64500) to confirm.
ops_bot: ACTIONS: 1) Reroute new requests away from sfo1 via smart-routing (enabled). 2) Failover policy to secondary region (sf2) in progress. 3) Notify customers on status page.
alice_ops: executing reroute now. command:
```
redwood-route override --from sfo1 --to sf2 --policy immediate
```
should take ~30s to propagate.
ben_sre: Confirming prefix withdraws suppressed. KV caches might still point to sfo1 for some sessions, expect gradual recovery.
chris_support: Drafting customer DM: 
```
Hi — we’re investigating an issue impacting some requests originating from our sfo1 region. You may see failed requests or increased latency. We’ve enabled an automatic reroute and are monitoring for recovery. We’ll update via status.redwood.ai and here with ETA. Sorry for the disruption. — Redwood Support
```
Can someone review?
sofia: LGTM. Add note for customers on Dedicated that they are unaffected unless they explicitly chose sfo1 egress.
ellen_pm: also add guidance for SDK users to set region: "us-west-2" or remove region pin to pick a healthy region.
ben_sre: provider responding: they've identified a partial interface saturation on sfo-edge-2 causing asymmetric egress. They will rebalance routes. Estimated mitigation 10-20m.
statusbot: STATUSPAGE: Draft update created (pending review):
```
Incident: Partial egress failures in sfo1
Impact: Some customers in western US may experience errors or increased latency for inference requests.
Current status: Mitigation in progress. Automatic reroute to sf2 enabled. Working with transit provider to restore full capacity.
Next update: in 15 minutes or upon significant change.
```

sofia: Suggested wording for customer-facing page: short, concrete, and include workaround. Add: "Workaround: Users can set region to sf2 or remove region pin to allow auto-routing."
chris_support: Can legal review the DM wording? @law_team any concerns about phrasing (no SLA admission beyond we are investigating)?
law_team: quick look — fine. avoid absolutes like "no data loss" unless verified. Recommend: "We are investigating and have applied a mitigation."
ben_sre: update: transit reports partial convergence at 10:18 UTC, traffic shifting back. Monitoring for error rate drop.
alice_ops: error rate across sfo1 decreased ~70% after route rebalance. still higher than baseline. continuing to monitor.
sofia: Internal comms template (for eng and cs) — keeping short: 
```
SFO1 Egress Incident — <current status summary>
Impact: description, affected features/regions
Mitigation: routing override to sf2 and transit provider rebalancing
Action items: CS DMs posted; status page updated; on-call continuing monitoring
Owner: ben_sre (ops), next handoff: alice_ops at shift change
```
Can we paste that into #general?
ellen_pm: yes, cc: support on the public post so they can copy/paste to customers.
chris_support: posted to affected customers who DM'ed us. Template used and added ticket refs + contact.
ben_sre: still seeing some session affinity to sfo1 causing a few residual failures — plan: graceful cache invalidation and increase KV TTL refresh to force rebind. Rolling now.
ops_bot: ROLLOUT: kv-sync invalidation started (10:28 UTC). Expect <5 minutes for most sessions to rebalance.
alice_ops: good, error rate now down ~90% vs peak. Greenish.
sofia: status page update suggestion for next update: mark "Mitigated" when error rates back to normal and transit confirms stable paths.
statusbot: STATUSPAGE UPDATE: set status to "Monitoring" and note mitigation steps taken.
ben_sre: transit confirms stable peering at 10:35 UTC, no further interface saturations. Moving to Monitoring.
chris_support: customers notified that mitigation applied and we're monitoring. No escalations pending.
ellen_pm: prepare follow-up postmortem template and customer-facing summary for <24h. I'll own the summary draft.
sofia: handoff: ben_sre -> alice_ops for next-hour watch. alice, you have the pager if anything regresses.
alice_ops: taking handoff. will keep watch for next 2 hours, will escalate immediately if error rate climbs >5% above baseline.
be_nice: (reaction) :thumbsup:
law_team: filing note for legal record with incident id INC-2198765432. Please attach timeline after postmortem.
ben_sre: quick notes for timeline (to paste into postmortem): detection 10:03 UTC, provider flap 10:04-10:18, reroute enabled 10:05, transit rebalance 10:18, kv invalidation 10:28, monitoring 10:35.
sofia: thanks all. once alice confirms 2h stable we can close incident and post short status update.
alice_ops: will update here at 12:35 UTC with final closure or earlier if healed.
statusbot: INCIDENT LOGGED: INC-2198765432.
